svg.title: Renal physiology: all lecture pathways, stimulus to effect, with negative feedback
svg.desc: One integrated left-to-right vector map. Shared hormones and brain outputs are connected. Important receptors, proteins and locations are retained; cAMP and phosphorylation-site details are omitted.

g.text: STIMULATION ON THE LEFT → EFFECT ON THE RIGHT | Shared nodes are connected; crossings without a dot are not junctions.
Key structures, receptors and transport proteins retained. Intracellular signalling / phosphorylation-site details omitted.
CONCENTRATING APPARATUS — generates, preserves and uses the medullary gradient
WHEN THE PATHWAY FAILS — disorders included in the lecture
FB1 Osmolality restored → osmotic VP / thirst stimulus decreases
FB2 Volume / BP recover → atrial / arterial firing recovers → non-osmotic VP + SNS drive ↓; renal perfusion improves → renin drive ↓
FB3 Plasma K⁺ restored → K⁺-driven aldosterone stimulus ↓†
FB4 Excess water removed → low-osmolality stimulus resolves
Solid coloured arrows = forward pathways. Red dashed flat-ended arrows = NEGATIVE FEEDBACK. Dashed taupe = lecture-specific VP–macula-densa model.
* Macula-densa V₁a → NO / PGE₂ → renin is the lecture model; net renin also reflects perfusion, NaCl delivery and pressure / volume feedback.
† Supporting physiology added for complete connections: JG β₁ input, direct K⁺–aldosterone control, ANGII–renin feedback and distal acid-excretion links.
PVN / SON produce VP; posterior-pituitary terminals release it. SFO / OVLT are sensory sites; PVN / SON also have intrinsic osmosensitivity.
MnPO = median preoptic nucleus; NTS = nucleus of the solitary tract; CVLM inhibits RVLM. M = magnocellular; parvocellular PVN provides the central SNS branch.
Source: Dr J Chu, BBMS2006 (Renal — student version), PDF pp. 3–15, 19–46; relevant classroom cardiovascular / saline material. AQP2 needs an intact medullary gradient.
Same named structures in different rows are the same anatomical sites. Water concentration, total Na⁺, ECF volume and arterial BP are related but distinct variables.
